rounds.text: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation, highlighted by a P/E ratio of just 4.54x and a price-to-book ratio of 0.46x against a book value of ₹ 215 [E1, E2]. This asset-rich profile is further underscored by the fact that the market value of its investments at ₹ 1,211 Cr exceeds its total market capitalization of ₹ 728 Cr [E3, E54]. Profitability has surged dramatically, with TTM profit growth reaching 24% and 3-year compounded profit growth hitting 79%, driven by an operating margin expansion of 23 percentage points over three years to 13% [E14, E15, E24]. This fundamental outperformance is confirmed by a scanX signal engine score of 89 out of 100, which notes recent tailwinds including a 19% YoY sales increase and a 410% YoY net profit jump [E59, E60, E62]. A discounted cash flow model suggests a massive intrinsic value of ₹ 462 per share yielding a 78.7% margin of safety, while a reverse DCF implies the current price of ₹ 98.7 is pricing in an overly pessimistic -4.5% earnings growth [E38, E39, E40]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10 years stands at -2% and the company is currently not paying out a dividend [E4, E8].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 4.54x, a price-to-book of 0.46x, and a market capitalization of ₹ 728 Cr [E1, E2, E3]. However, the low valuation is reflective of secular stagnation, as 10-year compounded sales growth is -2% and 10-year compounded profit growth is also -2% [E8, E12]. While the market value of investments is cited at ₹ 1,211 Cr [E54], this asset buffer has failed to translate into shareholder returns over the long term, given that compounded share price growth over 10 years sits at -10% [E16] and the worst peak-to-trough drawdown reaches -87.6% [E46]. Furthermore, despite reporting recent profit surges [E15, E62], the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], with filed statements explicitly flagging it as a negative that repeated profits are not distributed to shareholders [E55]. The operating-margin trend is flagged as inconsistent over the last two years [E26], and working capital days have experienced a severe deterioration from -87.7 days to 202 days [E58]. Finally, borrowings have jumped to Rs 85 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 40 Cr a year earlier [E33], increasing financial leverage alongside a low median return on equity of 5% over the last 3 years [E22] and 3% over the last 5 years [E21].
